title: Aggregate and group with GROUP BY / HAVING
description: Write a query that returns each `department_id` and the average salary in that department (as `avg_salary`, rounded to 2 decimals), but only for departments with more than 1 employee.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: GROUP BY, combined with an aggregate function and HAVING

GROUP BY column collapses rows sharing the same value into one group per value, which aggregate functions like AVG() and COUNT() then summarize - HAVING filters on those aggregated results, the way WHERE filters individual rows.
GROUP BY department_id, select AVG(salary) and COUNT(*), and add HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 to keep only departments with more than one employee.
expected_behavior: Returns department_id and avg_salary for departments with 2+ employees.
solution:
SELECT department_id, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_salary
FROM employees
GROUP BY department_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
explanation: WHERE can't filter on an aggregate like COUNT(*) because it runs before grouping happens - HAVING exists specifically to filter groups after GROUP BY and the aggregate functions have already run.
